title: The ITIL Value System and Governance

header.html: Know the five components of the ITIL Value System and explain its purpose; define governance and explain its enabling nature and activities; define operating model; explain how the organization's purpose and operating model are supported by the value chain activities and management practices
the official ITIL Foundation (Version 5) syllabus, version 5.0 (February 2026), categories 4.1, 4.3, 4.4.9 and 4.4.12

html:
1The ITIL Value System

The ITIL Value System (ITIL VS) describes how all the components and activities of an organization work together to enable value creation from demand (opportunity) to value.

Five components:

# Component Role
1 Guiding principles Recommendations that guide an organization in all circumstances
2 Governance How the organization is directed and controlled
3 Value chain The activities (the eight lifecycle activities) that turn demand into value
4 Management practices Sets of organizational resources for doing work or reaching an objective
5 Continual improvement Recurring improvement of everything, at all levels

Purpose: to ensure the organization continually co-creates value with all stakeholders through the use of products and services.

Old wording ITIL 4 named this the service value system (SVS). In Version 5 it is the ITIL Value System. [Verify live]

Exam tip

. Five components: principles, governance, value chain, practices, improvement. Remember P-G-V-P-I. The four dimensions and PESTLE are not components of the Value System.

2Governance

Governance is the means by which an organization is directed and controlled.

Idea Meaning
Enabling nature Governance does not block work; it enables the organization to achieve its objectives in the right way, by setting direction and boundaries
Activities Evaluate the current and future position, direct by setting policies and plans, monitor performance and conformance

Governance applies at all levels and links the Value System to the organization's purpose.

Exam tip

. Evaluate, direct, monitor. Governance directs and controls; management runs the day-to-day work.

3Operating model

An operating model describes how an organization is set up and works to deliver value: its structure, processes, people, technology and partners. It turns strategy into action.

The organization's purpose and operating model are supported by the value chain activities (the work that produces value) and the management practices (the resources and know-how used inside those activities). [Verify live]

Exam tip

. Governance directs and controls; management runs the work. An option that says governance replaces management, or only applies to the board, is wrong.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which list names the five components of the ITIL Value System?

  • APlan, improve, engage, design and transition, deliver and support
  • BOrganizations and people, information and technology, partners and suppliers, value streams and processes
  • CGuiding principles, governance, value chain, management practices, continual improvement
  • DPolitical, economic, social, technological, legal, environmental
Show the answer

Answer: C. Option B is the ITIL 4 value chain, C the dimensions, D PESTLE.

S2Which statement about governance is CORRECT? (1) Governance is how an organization is directed and controlled. (2) Governance is an enabling activity. (3) Governance only applies to the board and never to teams. (4) Governance replaces management.

  • A1 and 2
  • B3 and 4
  • C2 and 3
  • D1 and 4
Show the answer

Answer: A. Governance directs and controls, and it enables.

S3Which three activities does governance include?

  • ADiscover, design, build
  • BAcquire, transition, support
  • CEvaluate, direct, monitor
  • DPlan, improve, engage
Show the answer

Answer: C. Governance evaluates, directs and monitors.

S4Identify the missing word(s). The ITIL [ ? ] describes how all the components and activities of an organization work together to enable value creation.

  • AValue stream map
  • BService level agreement
  • CValue System
  • DPractice guide
Show the answer

Answer: C. That is the ITIL Value System.

S5A company describes its structure, processes, people, technology and partners and how they deliver value. What is this?

  • AAn operating model
  • BA product prototype
  • CA known error
  • DAn SLA
Show the answer

Answer: A. That description is an operating model.

S6In ITIL 4 this concept was called the service value system. What is it called in Version 5?

  • AThe four dimensions model
  • BThe lifecycle loop
  • CThe ITIL Value System
  • DThe practice map
Show the answer

Answer: C. The Version 5 name is the ITIL Value System.

4.2 Recall questions

R1Name the five components of the ITIL Value System.

Show the answer

Guiding principles, governance, value chain, management practices, continual improvement.

R2What is the purpose of the ITIL Value System?

Show the answer

To ensure the organization continually co-creates value with its stakeholders.

R3Define governance.

Show the answer

The means by which an organization is directed and controlled.

R4Name the governance activities.

Show the answer

Evaluate, direct and monitor.

R5What is an operating model?

Show the answer

How an organization is set up and works to deliver value.

R6What did ITIL 4 call the ITIL Value System?

Show the answer

The service value system.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact

Purpose continually co-create value
Governance direct and control; evaluate, direct, monitor; enabling
Operating model how the organization is set up to deliver value
